minutes.headline: Committee heard space pitches from three community groups and sent layout feedback on the TCP plan to the architect.
minutes.summary: The committee heard requests for space in the TC Passios building from the Boys and Girls Club, the cable access group (PAC) and the Lions Club food pantry. It reviewed an updated adjacency plan from the architect. Members and the town manager objected to the town manager's office being separated from the other town offices. It voted to send an outreach letter, approved three sets of minutes, and agreed to a placeholder presentation article for the fall special town meeting.

public_comment.topic: The chair asked for public comment and none was offered.
A member announced that the town charter has been signed by the governor and returned to Lunenburg, and that the Parks Commission will fill seats.
Presented the club's case for moving into the TCP building, citing three sites, security, the walk to the club, and a need for four to five thousand square feet.

public_comment.stated_role: former Boys and Girls Club board member
public_comment.topic: Spoke in support of the club's request for space at TCP.
Spoke on PAC's studio needs: contiguous space, public access day and night, higher ceilings, and about 2600 square feet. Asked that agendas be posted on the town website.
Asked for a first-floor home for the Lions Club food pantry, now in the public safety building attic, plus meeting and meal space.

votes.motion: Authorize the chair to send the drafted outreach letter, with the revisions discussed, to the Ledger and post it elsewhere as appropriate.

passed; roll call with one abstention

decisions.decision: The chair will invite the superintendent to a future meeting to discuss school offices.

what_happened.line: The committee voted unanimously on roll call to send a drafted community outreach letter, with revisions, to the Ledger and post it elsewhere as appropriate.
Members and the town manager objected to the architect's updated adjacency plan, which separates the town manager's office from the other town offices.
The chair will send a time-stamped video clip to the architect to pass on the committee's feedback on the plan.
The committee heard space requests for the TCP building from the Boys and Girls Club, the cable access group (PAC) and the Lions Club food pantry.
A placeholder presentation article will be prepared for the fall special town meeting, worded like the annual town meeting article.

why_it_matters: The layout of the TCP building decides which town offices and community groups get space there, and so how the building serves residents and what it may later cost to build and run.
The placeholder article suggests residents may be asked to vote on the project at the fall special town meeting.
